albums.blurb: BADBADNOTGOOD are a Toronto trio — Matthew Tavares on keys, Chester Hansen on bass, and Alex Sowinski on drums — who first drew attention reworking hip-hop material by artists like MF DOOM and Odd Future as live jazz. III, released in 2014 on Innovative Leisure, was their first album of entirely original compositions and is fully instrumental, arriving just before they began adding guest vocalists on later records like IV.
albums.reception: The album was longlisted for the 2014 Polaris Music Prize and holds a score of 72 (“generally favorable”) on Metacritic.

albums.blurb: Ventura is Anderson .Paak's fourth studio album, released on 12 Tone/Aftermath in April 2019 only five months after Oxnard, and it swings back from that record's rap-heavy sound toward smooth, live-band soul. Made with Dr. Dre as executive producer, it features André 3000, Smokey Robinson, Brandy, Jazmine Sullivan, Lalah Hathaway, and a posthumous Nate Dogg appearance.
albums.reception: It debuted at number four on the Billboard 200 — his first US top-ten album — and won Best R&B Album at the 2020 Grammy Awards.

albums.blurb: Beverly Glenn-Copeland is a Philadelphia-born, classically trained musician who moved to Canada in 1961, studied at McGill, and spent decades in children's television — twenty-five years as a regular on Mr. Dressup and writing for Sesame Street. He self-released this third album from his home in Huntsville, Ontario in 1986, recording it on just a Yamaha DX7 synthesizer and a Roland TR-707 drum machine, setting his warm, low voice against minimalist electronic patterns.
albums.reception: Only about two dozen cassette copies sold on release, but a Japanese rare-record collector's rediscovery of the album three decades later set off a revival that brought remastered vinyl reissues in 2017, an international touring career in Glenn-Copeland's seventies, and the 2019 documentary Keyboard Fantasies: The Beverly Glenn-Copeland Story.
